on_off.help: On or off: on or 1, off or 0.

framing.help: The reply framing: on for JSON-RPC, off for text.

address.help: A memory address in hex, 0x optional, at most eight digits.

block.help: A block length in bytes, 1 to 64.

hex_bytes.help: Bytes as hex pairs, spaces allowed between pairs.

mask.help: A mask in hex, no prefix; its digit count is the width: 2, 4 or 8.

help.help: The board's commands, each name mapped to its one-line help; help <command> answers that command's line.

json.help: Set the reply framing, on for JSON-RPC or off for text; bare json reads it.
json.long_help: json off switches the board to text replies: every reply after it is text, not JSON, until json on, or any request line starting with {, switches back.  The config sends json on at every connect.

xmodem.help: Transfer a file over XMODEM: xmodem recv receives into the board buffer, xmodem send streams it back; bare xmodem reads the buffered byte count.
xmodem.long_help: The transfer itself is driven from the host by /xfer.xmodem.send and /xfer.xmodem.recv; this command only puts the board into receive or send mode. The reply after a transfer is the byte count. XMODEM pads the last block, so a received count is a multiple of 128.

typed_args.name: mode
typed_args.help: recv, send, or empty to read the buffered byte count.

led.help: Turn the onboard LED on or off; bare led reads it.  The reply is the state, on or off.

temp.help: Read the on-chip temperature sensor, in degrees Celsius, as a number.

id.help: The board's unique ID in hex, which is also its USB serial number.

machine.help: List the names in MicroPython's machine module: its classes, functions and constants.
machine.long_help: The board answers by looking, so the list is what this build of MicroPython has.  machine.<name> on a class lists that class's names the same way: machine.Pin answers the pin constants and methods.  A JSON request carries the same: method machine.Pin.value, params [2, 1].

machine..help: Read or call a name under machine on the board: machine.freq, machine.Pin.value 2 1.
machine..long_help: The board finds the dotted name by attribute and answers it, calling it with the values when it is a function; the line is names and values, never Python.  A method reached through its class takes the object's id as its first value: machine.Pin.value 2 1 is Pin(2).value(1).  A value is a number (decimal or 0x hex), a quoted string, a path such as machine.Pin.OUT, or name=value.  A number, string or list answers as itself, bytes as uppercase hex, a class as its names, anything else as Python prints it.  Every name machine has is in reach with nothing checked first: machine.reset restarts the board and machine.bootloader leaves MicroPython, so this entry is destructive and an MCP agent is asked to confirm each call with you.

typed_args.name: call
typed_args.help: What follows machine.: a dotted name, then its values separated by spaces.

MEM.R.help: Read memory at an address: rows of hex bytes, then OK.  Prefer /mem.read, which checks the address first.
MEM.R.long_help: The board reads whatever address it is given.  One the chip cannot reach resets it, and reading a peripheral register can change it (a FIFO pops).  /mem.read names registers from the device file and refuses sweeps of peripheral space.

MEM.W.help: Write bytes to memory at an address, then OK.  Prefer /mem.write, which checks the address first.
MEM.W.long_help: The board writes whatever address it is given; one the chip cannot reach resets it.

MEM.M.help: Masked write with interrupts off, word = (word & and) | or; the reply is the word before, then OK.
MEM.M.long_help: The masks have the same digit count, which sets the width (2, 4 or 8 for a byte, a half or a word), and the address is aligned to it.  /mem.write X.bit and /mem.or use it.

MEM.INFO.help: The memory interface: block limit, address width, byte order, and whether MEM.M is there.
